methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $690M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Bethlehem Steel Corp is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $690M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 companies in Robotics & Manufacturing—1 public (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

A Stage-Progression method was applied, using total capital raised ($690M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of transitions beyond Growth stage, yielding $828M. Peer-Median triangulation could not be applied: while 11 same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints, making a narrow peer median unreliable. An all-sector median was rejected as potentially misleading given the heterogeneity across robotics subsegments.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $704M to $952M, with a median of $828M based on stage-progression alone. This represents a single-method conclusion; material uncertainty surrounds the valuation absent a sufficient set of tightly-filtered peer comparables. Key risks to this range include: (1) the reliability of raised capital as a valuation proxy absent portfolio company outcomes, and (2) the absence of narrowly comparable transaction data in this sector-stage combination. Additional comparable transactions or observable revenue/EBITDA multiples would materially narrow this range.
